correctness.rationale: With ||r_0||=1 and β_j>0 through k, T_j=I+iJ_j is invertible because its Hermitian part is I. Widlund residual r_j is a multiple of the next Lanczos vector, and the corner cofactor gives ||r_j||=∏_{l≤j}β_l/|D_j|. The nonzero Galerkin residuals for j=0,…,k are orthogonal and affinely span r_0−AK_k; minimizing the norm of an affine combination gives the Rapoport inverse-square sum, also verified in Higgins–Reed–Szyld Eq. (10). Equality with the min residual bound means every Widlund norm equals one. The continuant D_j=(1+ia_j)D_{j−1}+β_{j−1}²D_{j−2} then gives |z_j|=β_j for z_j=D_j/D_{j−1}, so z_j=1+ia_j+conj(z_{j−1}) and Re(z_j)=j, starting at z_1=1+ia_1. Thus β_j≥j. With the positive unit Perron vector w of B_k and its alternating-sign copy, the two Rayleigh quotients of the leading block are d±2∑β_j w_j w_{j+1}, where d is their common diagonal contribution. The larger absolute quotient is at least 2∑β_jw_jw_{j+1}≥ρ_k, with strict inequality if any coupling is greater than j. The full norm bounds this compression. B_k attains the bound by the factorial continuant and sign symmetry of its spectrum. In dimension k+1, equality forces every β_j=j and hence a_1,…,a_k=0 by the quotient recurrence; the two Rayleigh quotients then differ from ±ρ_k by a_{k+1}w_{k+1}², forcing a_{k+1}=0. Valid for exact arithmetic, common initial iterate and the specified no-breakdown setup; no near-saturation rate is established. value.rationale: A sharp example by itself does not say whether the worst comparison factor can arise with a small skew part. The theorem makes the skew spectral norm a necessary resource for exact saturation, gives an attainable barrier at each iteration, and singles out the minimal-dimensional system that uses the least such norm. This is a natural structural and extremal question following the original comparison, not just another verification of its saturating example.
